subject: Performance + multi-region routing follow-up (HealthSync)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Murphy <alice.murphy@healthsync.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: perf targets, streaming, and routing questions (HealthSync)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size a pilot and put together an SLO proposal: 

1) Target latency (p95) you mentioned as a goal for the user-facing transcript/assist flows — can you confirm numbers per region? (US, EU, APAC)
2) Throughput profile: sustained qps vs burst qps; typical request size / avg tokens; are there heavy back-to-back bursts tied to batch jobs?
3) Concurrency: any expected long-lived sessions (websocket/streaming) vs short request-response?
4) Streaming requirements: did you need chunked/real-time streaming for transcripts and partial-turn replies? Max chunk latency?
5) Data residency: EU customer data must stay in EU — confirm whether logs/metrics / debug traces can be replicated to US for ops.

If you can poke the attached traffic sample and privacy doc and reply inline that would be perfect.

Next steps I propose: Redwood will draft a two-week pilot config (EU canary + US primary) with target SLOs + cost estimate once we have the throughput numbers. Can we aim to reconvene Thu (5/27) for 30m to align?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Attachments: call-recording.mp3 (stated), healthsync-traffic-sample.json (requested)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Murphy <alice.murphy@healthsync.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: perf targets, streaming, and routing questions (HealthSync)

Hi Alice / Marissa — jumping in with a few technical clarifications that will determine how we configure batching, KV cache, and routing policies for the pilot: 

- Typical request shape: avg prompt tokens and avg generated tokens (separate numbers). If you have a 95th percentile token length distribution even better.
- QPS profile: please indicate sustained qps, peak qps (1-min and 5-min peaks). Also indicate whether peaks are regional-local or global-fanout.
- Streaming: you said live transcripts with partial results — what's the max tolerable partial-chunk delay? We typically target <150ms chunk emission for interactive UIs but can tune.
- Concurrency: are there expected long-lived websockets (concurrency measured as active KV sessions) — approximate counts per region.
- Failover preference: if EU region is unavailable, do you want automatic US failover for latency (violates sovereignty) or prefer degraded mode with queued requests?

I've attached an SLO matrix template (slo-matrix-template.xlsx) — fill in the cells and we can map to a Dedicated vs Hosted config.

Technical signature:
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Attachments: slo-matrix-template.xlsx

From: Alice Murphy <alice.murphy@healthsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: perf targets, streaming, and routing questions (HealthSync)

Thanks Marissa / Tessa — answers inline below and attached a small sample of our traffic profile plus our privacy policy.

- Request sizes: avg prompt tokens ~ 45; avg generated tokens ~ 85; 95th percentile prompt 210 tokens, generated 420 tokens (we include some long-case summarizations).
- QPS profile: sustained 50 qps globally; peak bursts up to 200 qps sustained for 3–7 minutes; peaks are usually US-originated but can spike in EU during local business hours.
- Streaming: yes — partial chunk delivery required. Max acceptable chunk delay ~ 250ms; finalization latency target (p95) should be under 120ms in US, under 180ms in EU, and under 220ms in APAC for interactive flows.
- Concurrency: we expect up to ~500 active sessions at peak globally, with ~320 simultaneously active from US, ~120 EU, ~60 APAC. Many of these keep an open websocket for 30–90s.
- Data residency: EU customer transcripts and PII must remain in EU. APAC (Japan + Australia) must remain in APAC. Aggregated telemetry and anonymized metrics can be replicated to US for ops; raw logs with PII should not leave region.

Attached: healthsync-traffic-sample.json, healthsync-privacy-policy.pdf

Let us know if these targets are achievable. We are particularly sensitive to EU sovereignty and would prefer queued degraded mode over automatic cross-region failover that moves raw transcripts.

— Alice Murphy
Head of Product Operations, HealthSync
alice.murphy@healthsync.com
Attachments: healthsync-traffic-sample.json, healthsync-privacy-policy.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Murphy <alice.murphy@healthsync.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: perf targets, streaming, and routing questions (HealthSync)

Alice — great detail, thank you. Short summary and proposed next steps from Redwood: 

Summary of feasibility based on your numbers:
- Latency: US p95 <120ms — feasible on our Hosted+Dedicated hybrid with streaming-optimized kernels and aggressive KV prefix caching for small-turn interactions.
- EU p95 <180ms / APAC p95 <220ms — feasible with regional routing + local model variants; we will recommend EU and APAC dedicated pools for the initial pilot to maintain sovereignty and reduce cross-region RTT.
- Throughput & concurrency: sustained 50 qps / 200 qps peaks and ~500 concurrent sessions — we recommend a pilot capacity commit that provisions for 1.5x peak to cover autoscale buffers.
- Streaming: we can meet ~200–250ms chunk emission with our streaming path; will run a short bench to validate 150–250ms under your token distributions.
- Data residency: we will honor EU/APAC in-region storage for transcripts and raw logs. Anonymized metrics can be aggregated to US ops. We will not configure automatic cross-region failover for PII data; instead propose a queued degraded mode and alerting policy.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to share a two-week pilot SLO proposal (attached: redwood_slo-proposal.pdf) that maps your p95 targets to config and suggested Dedicated pool sizes.
2) Technical bench: Tessa will run a 2-day bench using your attached traffic sample to validate chunk emission and p95 across regions (ETA: 5 business days after confirmation).
3) Legal/Proc: Marissa will send a narrow SOC / data residency addendum request for the pilot contract.
4) Sync: 30-minute call Thu 5/29 at 10:00am PT to review pilot proposal and bench results. Please confirm availability.

If that plan works I will loop in our licensing team and prep a draft MSA addendum for the pilot. Thanks again — we know the EU residency constraint is critical and will treat that as a hard requirement for the pilot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Attachments: redwood_slo-proposal.pdf
